data.narrative:
Neura Robotics, founded by David Reger, is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $1.4B to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 9 private robotics firms plus 1 public comparable, spanning late-stage (Series D) and mid-stage (Series B) financings across the sector.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $1.4B total raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $2.4B. Peer-median analysis examines seven same-sector comparables at adjacent stages—including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D)—producing a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B.

The two methods yield a triangulated range of $1.4B (low), $2.0B (median), and $2.7B (high). The stage-progression method's higher result reflects potential Series C momentum, while the peer-median anchors valuation to observed market pricing for similar-stage companies. Key uncertainties include the relative maturity of Neura's commercial traction versus the peer cohort and any proprietary technology or unit economics that would justify a premium or discount to sector medians.
